extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting manuscripts to Cambridge journals (manuscript authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for manuscript authors on composing Data Availability Statements (DAS): what DAS are, what counts as data, where to place the statement, how to preserve anonymity for double-blind review, and exemplar wording for common data-access situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and definition of a Data Availability Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Availability Statements are brief statements about whether the authors of an article have made the evidence supporting their findings available, and if so, where readers may access it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They’re not just for quantitative data – they can also be used to describe evidence such as qualitative materials and “data” in the broadest sense. Data Availability Statements help to promote transparency and reproducibility in research, and to increase the visibility of valuable evidence produced or gathered during the course of research. As part of our commitment to supporting open research, some of our journals now require all manuscripts to include a Data Availability Statement in order to be accepted for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation: state whether data/evidence are available and where/how
rubrics_metrics.description: A Data Availability Statement simply needs to state whether you have made evidence available, and if so, where and how it can be accessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not mean you must make all data publicly available; authors are encouraged to share when possible but may describe restricted access. If your chosen journal has additional requirements related to sharing data or other evidence, these will be specified in the journal’s instructions for authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: What counts as 'data'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Data' is interpreted in the broadest sense to mean any evidence or resources that would be necessary for others to fully evaluate the basis for your findings, and to verify or reproduce your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes raw or processed data sets, code, and protocols, as well as qualitative resources such as images, audio, video, maps, interview transcripts, field notes, and public reports. It also includes any information necessary for others to access, interpret and process these resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of the Data Availability Statement in the manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Availability Statements should generally be placed in the back matter of your manuscript, just before your References, unless your chosen journal specifies otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your journal uses a double-blind peer review process, ensure the information in your Data Availability Statement doesn't compromise author anonymity. If the DAS could identify authors, submit it the same way as any other identifying information (for example, as part of a Title Page or as a separate document) according to journal instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example status: Data openly available in a public repository with permanent identifier
rubrics_metrics.description: The data that support the findings of this study are openly available in [repository name] at http://doi.org/[doi], reference number [reference number].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the repository name and a persistent identifier (such as a DOI). Provide the exact link/doi and reference number to enable direct access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example status: Data embargoed due to commercial restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The data that support the findings of this study will be available in [repository name] at [URL / DOI link] following a [6 month] embargo from the date of publication, to allow for commercialisation of research findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the repository, the link/DOI if known, and the duration/reason for the embargo so readers know when data will become available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example status: Data available on request due to privacy/ethical restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The data that support the findings of this study are available on request from the corresponding author, [initials]. The data are not publicly available due to [restrictions e.g. their containing information that could compromise the privacy of research participants].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the contact (e.g., corresponding author initials) and clearly state the nature of the restriction (privacy, ethics). This explains why data are not public and provides a route for legitimate access requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example status: Data generated at a central, large-scale facility, available upon request
rubrics_metrics.description: Raw data were generated at [facility name]. Derived data supporting the findings of this study are available from the corresponding author [initials] on request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between raw data held by facilities and derived data the authors can provide; indicate who to contact for access and any facility-specific access processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example status: Data subject to third party restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The data that support the findings of this study are available from [third party]. Restrictions apply to the availability of these data, which were used under licence for this study. Data are available [from the authors / at URL] with the permission of [third party].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If data are licensed or held by third parties, identify the data holder and explain that permission is required; indicate how requests should be made (via the authors or directly to the third party).

rubrics_metrics.name: Example status: Data available within the article or its supplementary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors confirm that the data supporting the findings of this study are available within the article [and/or its supplementary materials].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When all necessary evidence is included in the article/supplementary files, state this clearly so readers know no external access is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example status: Data sharing not applicable – no new data generated
rubrics_metrics.description: Data availability is not applicable to this article as no new data were created or analysed in this study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this statement for articles such as reviews, commentaries, or theory pieces where no underlying data were generated or analysed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example status: Data available on request from the authors (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The data that support the findings of this study are available from the corresponding author, [author initials], upon reasonable request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A generic 'available upon reasonable request' statement should identify a contact and imply that access will be considered; combine with any information about restrictions or conditions for access where relevant.
